title: After disasters
hookLine: Sikh volunteers cook and clean after floods and fires
tomorrow: the fire's out. the hills are black. who plants them back?

cards: A wildfire is burning in the hills two towns over. At noon the sky is orange and smells like a campfire nobody wanted. Harjit's trucks are loading pallets of water for the evacuation center at a high school gym.
Simran rides along. When they pull in, Sikh volunteers have already set up gas burners in the parking lot. Big pots.
Dal, rice, roti, tea. A sign in marker: free hot food, everyone welcome.

teach.h: LANGAR DOESN'T ASK WHO YOU ARE.
teach.b: Sikh volunteers have cooked and cleaned after floods and fires, and the reason is an old one on this path: langar doesn't ask who you are.

teach.h: SARBAT DA BHALA: THE GOOD OF ALL.
teach.b: Ardas, as the Sikh code of conduct gives it, ends with a phrase that holds the whole idea: sarbat da bhala, the good of all. Not the good of Sikhs. The good of all.
So after a disaster, the seva is mostly simple. Show up.

teach.h: BRING WHAT YOU HAVE. ASK. STAY.
teach.b: Bring what you have: water, a pot, a truck, two hands. Ask what's needed instead of guessing. Stay after the cameras leave.

teach.h: A WEEK OF SEVA IN ONE PARKING LOT.
teach.b: And look how this whole week fits into one parking lot. Start at home: Harjit's own trucks. Beyond the walls: a gym full of strangers.
Langar everywhere: the pots on the burners. Sit with them: Bebe on a folding chair beside a man whose street was evacuated. Company for the old: she doesn't leave him.
Teach freely: Dev, who came with Kiran, showing a younger kid how to fold napkins.

how: Sikh volunteers and gurdwaras set up langar and relief after floods, fires and other disasters, serving anyone in need; Ardas ends with a prayer for sarbat da bhala, the good of all.

games.q: a flood hits a town an hour away. you can't drive and you have no money to give. what does show up mean for you?
o: ask what's needed and offer what you have: time, hands, a phone call.
nothing yet; seva after disasters is for people with trucks.
post about it a lot, so other people will show up instead.
games.why: show up means bring what you have and ask what's needed. two hands and a phone count; sarbat da bhala is for everyone to carry.

practice: Name one kind of emergency that could reach your town: a fire, a flood, a storm, a long power cut. Name one thing you could bring or do if it came, and the one obstacle most likely to stop you.
Then choose one small step past that obstacle, and let it rest while you sit.

wordCard.voice: After disasters. Seva when floods and fires come: showing up for the good of all. Sarbat da bhala.

orig.note: Punjabi: sarbat da bhala, the good of all; the closing words of Ardas.

carryVoice: Your line: show up. Water, a pot, two hands, for the good of all. Next week, more seva.
